static_traits.name: Lin Haoran
static_traits.family_status: Only child; the family keeps 3 cats
static_traits.medical_history: without major physical illness history; not yet had similar problems before, not yet received psychological counseling/treatment
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, slightly reserved, tending to focus on mistakes and Self-doubt, acceptable cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I feel my dancing ability is not important, because anyone with two feet can do it, which makes me feel negated and undervalue my ability.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this feeling of being negated has begun affecting my enjoyment of dance and my self-esteem.
growth_experiences: Starting years ago to frequently receive praise for dancing, while experiencing the pressure of moving to a new city (new school, new friends, sudden environment change); gradually developing distrust of praise and a sense of being negated, believing 'anyone can dance', with worsening Self-doubt when praised and constant Reinforcement.

core_beliefs: My strengths and achievements do not count / are not worth recognizing
I am not good enough, the praise is not real

special_situations.event: After the dance showcase ended, someone praised her performance to her face as 'great / wonderful'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there is any mistake or imperfection in a performance, I do not deserve praise, the praise must not be real
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Accepts with a surface smile, devalues the positive feedback inside, avoids acknowledging her own strengths
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite, I am actually deceiving them.

special_situations.event: When others usually praise her dancing ability
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others praise, it is often just out of politeness or social need, not trustworthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Guessing others' motives, negating positive information, avoiding positive self-evaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just saying nice things, not really thinking so.

special_situations.event: Reviewing one's performance after a show, noticing several mistakes made
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Mistakes mean the overall performance is very Average or even a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Only focusing on mistakes and inadequacy, ignoring well-done parts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I performed awkwardly, mistakes show I am no good.

special_situations.event: After moving to a new city, faces a new school, new friends, and a new environment
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel out of place in the new environment, it shows my dancing is not that special, nor truly recognized
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowers self-evaluation, is skeptical of praise, reduces motivation to dance to avoid disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Here my dancing is nothing, everyone can do it.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be truly seen and affirmed, appreciated as a Dancer
core_conflict.fear: Fearing praise is not real, the shame and negation of being exposed as 'not good enough'
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of being exposed and shamed by devaluing positive feedback and focusing on errors
Maintains a psychologically safe distance, avoiding the disappointment brought by attachment and expectations

object_relations.self_representation: A flawed performer who may be an 'impostor'
object_relations.object_representation: Seemingly friendly but unreliable judges who praise casually out of politeness

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others invite him to acknowledge strengths and review what was done well
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that admitting strengths equals self-deception, and being seen through would bring more shame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Restrained tone, emphasizing facts and mistake details, weakening emotional expression, using 'objective analysis' to negate the positive.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving direct praise or positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets others' kindness as polite, false praise
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Saying 'everyone can / this is nothing' in a flat tone, diluting praise with social etiquette or universality Interpretations.

manifestations: Believing 'anyone with two feet can dance', thus negating the uniqueness and value of her own skill
When praised, feels like a 'fraud', finds it hard to experience the meaning of being seen and affirmed
Shaken self-positioning and worth after moving, feeling dance is 'nothing'
outcomes: Decreased dance motivation, daily routine affected
Avoiding accepting positive feedback, experiencing being negated and unreal

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Attributing her non-acceptance to 'the other is just being polite', negating the authenticity of praise
Assuming others' motives insincere when praised

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Over-focusing on mistakes and inadequacy, fearing being seen as 'fishing for compliments', unwilling to express insecurity to friends
When reviewing performance, mainly emphasizes mistakes and suppresses self-affirmation

positive_force: Dance skill receiving multiple positive feedback from others
Can notice and express one's own troubles; willing to seek help
Has several friends to confide in (though temporarily finds it hard to speak up)
negative_force: Cognitive style of negating positive information (Disqualifying the Positive)
Mind-reading-style inference of others' motives, focusing only on mistakes (Mental Filtering)
Discomfort and insecurity from moving and the new environment
Self-doubt worsening in praised situations, affecting motivation and daily life

target_behavior.behavior: Automatically negating positive feedback when praised for dancing, feeling 'like a fraud' and reducing practice/performance willingness
antecedent: Others' praise or positive feedback on their dancing
Facing new environments and new peers after moving to a new city
target_behavior.core_reason: Shaken sense of self-worth under relocation and adaptation pressure, forming the 'negate the positive' cognitive bias and worry about shame / being exposed
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential shame and exposure risk, maintaining the self-consistency of 'I am not that special'
target_behavior.consequence: Lowered self-esteem, decreased dance motivation affecting daily routine
